summary: Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard University (~1959–1963). He held posts at Harvard (1970–1978, 1998), UC Berkeley (~1972–1973), and Cornell University (~1978–1998).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under numerous teachers including Geshe Ngawang Samten, Lobsang Gyatso, and Robert A. F. Thurman. He has held professorships at Hampshire College, Smith College, UMass Amherst, and Melbourne.

Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1970–1975). He has held academic posts at the University of Essex (~1975–1997), Vanderbilt University (~1997–2001), and The New School (~2001).
Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1934–1938), where he was taught by M. H. Krishna (~1935–1938).

Jayandra Soni is an Indologist and philosopher who earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University. He taught at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and the University of Innsbruck (~2012–2017), and became Generalsekretär of the IASS in 2012.

Jaś Elsner is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at King's College, Cambridge, Courtauld Institute, and Harvard. His main posts include Courtauld Institute (~1992–1999), Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and Professor of Late Antique Art at Oxford (2014).
Jean Dantinne worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He taught at Suryavarman II School (1961–1962), directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966), and held research posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He served as director of studies at EPHE (1941–1978), held a chair at Collège de France (1951–1978), and directed EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indo-European linguistics. He studied at the University of Liège and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, later holding posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1974–1993), Liège (~1993–1994), and Collège de France (1993).

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Kern and Uhlenbeck at the University of Amsterdam. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and served as director at Leiden University (1914–1939) and the Kern Institute.

Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at ENFOM and EPHE under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss. He held professorships at INALCO (1913–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a French physicist and Indologist who studied at École Polytechnique under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace. He was a professor at École Centrale de Beauvais (1797), Collège de France (1800–1862), and the Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Paris and studied at École du Louvre. He served as director (1986–2004) and president (~1986–2008) of the Musée Guimet.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at Paris Nanterre (1967–1970), Paris 8 (1972–1987), UC Irvine (~1987–1998), and Emory University (~1995–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher. He was educated at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, Lycée du Parc, and the École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Jean-Louis Burnouf was a classical scholar who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy and Alexander Hamilton. He served as a professor at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1826) and held the chair of Latin eloquence at Collège de France (1816–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He has held a research post at the CNRS.
Jean-Luc Chevillard is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1975) under Antoine Culioli. He served as a researcher at the CNRS from ~1992 to 2021.

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied under Bernard Frank at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (1979), and served as director at Collège de France (2010–2022).
